name: gameplay-cinema-item
origin: An item drop and its pickup (checkpoint 4, slice b2), on the round of gameplay-cinema-bomb (seed 42, Arcade, Normal, Cinema, robot 0; the AI robots stopped at the round's first frame): the map-loading screen half way (loading: frame 670, LoadingMapUI's UI_reading 30 frames after START), the same walk, bomb and blast, then the broken box's drop roll (Box.createProp at frame 815: Math.random draws 412 and 413, SpeedProp) and its PixelClip (drop: frame 817, the first bitmap; idle: frame 826), the robot walking down onto it (approach: 847) and GetItemCommand eating it (pickup: 848).
godot_note: Godot starts on the recorded round with the original's Math.random place (tests/goldens/gameplay-cinema-start/math_random.json), so the box's drop roll draws the same numbers.

actions.godot_note: Godot cannot roll the original's board yet (its Math.random draws before the map are not reproduced): the round this START opens takes its board (every box's _brick5 frame, the layout's hold cells and portals) and the enemy robots from the golden of the cinema-start capture (App.round_as_recorded).
AIControl.stop through the original's own method (fixture); Godot gives the robot no commands, as it then has none.

wall_clock_text./@0#1/@0/time: Game.countTime counts Date seconds; the reference player's Date follows the host clock, not its stepped frames, so TIME reads 178 or 177 here depending on the machine

wall_clock_frame./@0#1/@0#1/processBarMc: LoadingMapUI.progress tweens processBarMc's frame with TweenMax, which the reference player runs on the host's clock, not its stepped frames: in one recording the bar reads 24 at frame 670, in another 46
